question: Got reject 22 on a Victoza claim, what now?
assumption: Assuming NY Medicaid (NYRx), since this is a claim reject question with no program named.
answer:
Assuming NY Medicaid: Victoza is preferred and in the BLTG program. NCPDP reject 22 means a missing or invalid DAW code.

1. Resubmit with DAW 9 (substitution allowed by prescriber, plan requests brand) in field 408-D8.
2. Don't send DAW 1 unless the prescriber wrote DAW and "Brand Medically Necessary" on the Rx. DAW 1 is the only exception.
3. No DAW or brand-necessary wording is needed on the Rx for BLTG drugs.

Generic liraglutide is non-preferred and needs PA. The GLP-1 class also has clinical criteria (CC). It needs PA if the patient is on a DPP-IV inhibitor at the same time.

ny_medicaid_pdl (NY Medicaid, binding, 2026-09-14)
NYRx Preferred Drug Program (PDP) Preferred Drug List > NYS Medicaid NYRx Brand Less Than Generic (BLTG) Program
[p 77]
On April 26, 2010, NYRx, the Medicaid Pharmacy Program, implemented a new cost-containment initiative, which promotes the use of certain multisource brand name drugs when the cost of the brand name drug is less expensive than the generic equivalent.
In conformance with State Education Law, which intends that patients receive the lower cost alternative, brand name drugs included in this program:
Do not require "Dispense as Written" (DAW) or "Brand Medically Necessary" on the prescription
Have a generic copayment
Are paid at the Brand Name Drug reimbursement rate or usual and customary price, whichever is lower (SMAC/FUL are not applied)
Do not require a new prescription if the drug is removed from this program
Bosulif ® tablet, Janumet ® , Januvia ® , and Xyrem ® will be added to the program
Farxiga ® and Ravicti ® will be removed from the program

Please keep in mind that drugs in this program may be subject to PA requirements of other pharmacy programs, promoting the use of the most cost-effective product.
[p 78]
Pursuant to this program, prescription claims submitted to the Medicaid program do not require the submission of Dispense as Written/Product Selection Code of '1'; Pharmacies should submit DAW code 9 (Substitution Allowed by Prescriber but Plan Requests Brand). Pharmacies will receive an NCPDP reject response of "22" which means missing/invalid DAW code if other DAW codes are submitted. The only exception to this is DAW code 1 and "Brand Medically Necessary" on the prescription.
